 League of Legends Worlds 2026 Final: Gen.G vs Bilibili Gaming Analysis and Preview
 Gen.G and Bilibili Gaming (BLG) meet tomorrow, Saturday, November 14, in the League of Legends World Championship final at Barclays Center in Brooklyn. The best-of-five is scheduled for 2 p.m. […]
 Laura Longo 
 Published: November 13th, 2026

 Gen.G and Bilibili Gaming (BLG) meet tomorrow, Saturday, November 14, in the League of Legends World Championship final at Barclays Center in Brooklyn. The best-of-five is scheduled for 2 p.m. ET (11 a.m. PT) . Gen.G swept both knockout opponents, while BLG beat three-time defending champion T1 to reach their second Worlds final.
 The Gen.G vs BLG prediction favours Gen.G to win the series. The LCK champions have dropped just one game at Worlds, but their semifinal sweep included a comeback from more than 4,000 gold down. BLG, meanwhile, won back-to-back games after T1 levelled their semifinal. Both teams have already had to adjust when a series stopped going their way.
 Korea vs China at the LoL Worlds 2026 Final
 Gen.G arrive in the final unbeaten in knockout play, with a 3-0 sweep of LYON in the quarterfinals and another 3-0 sweep of Invictus Gaming in the semifinals. BLG, meanwhile, swept Dplus KIA 3-0 and then beat T1 3-1, ending T1’s run of four straight Worlds finals.
 The stakes are significant for both sides. It is Gen.G’s first final under the Gen.G name and their first since Samsung Galaxy won in 2017, while BLG are back in a second final after losing to T1 in 2024. Anyone weighing the esports odds and betting markets for this series should note that it is also the first Worlds final without T1 since 2021.
 Gen.G vs BLG Recent Form and Road to the Final
 The two finalists took different routes through the Swiss Stage:
 Gen.G: went 3-0 in the Swiss Stage, then swept LYON 3-0 on November 4 and Invictus Gaming 3-0 on November 7.
 BLG: went 3-2 in the Swiss Stage (losses to Movistar KOI and Top Esports), then swept Dplus KIA 3-0 on November 5 and beat T1 3-1 on November 8.
 Gen.G dropped their only game at Worlds in a 2–1 Swiss Stage win over LYON, then swept them in the quarterfinals. In the semifinal, Gen.G came back from 6–0 down in kills in Game 3 to complete a 3–0 sweep of Invictus Gaming.
 BLG lost twice in Swiss and qualified with a 2–0 win over Hanwha Life Esports. They’ve since won six of seven knockout games, including a 3–1 semifinal win over T1 after the defending champions tied the series in Game 2.
 Gen.G vs BLG Head-to-Head Record
 Gen.G and BLG have met four times in Riot international best-of-fives, and the series is tied 2-2:
 MSI 2023: BLG won 3-0 in the lower bracket semifinal.
 Worlds 2023: BLG won 3-2 in the quarterfinals.
 MSI 2024: Gen.G won 3-1 in the upper bracket final.
 MSI 2024: Gen.G won 3-1 in the grand final.
 Treat that record as historical context: the bot lane was different at the time, with Peyz for Gen.G and Elk for BLG, and the two current starting fives have never met in a best-of-five.

 In his first Worlds final , Chovy faces Knight in a mid-lane matchup that could shape the early dragon fights. Whoever clears the wave first can help Canyon or Xun secure vision and set up in the river before the other team arrives.
 Ruler vs Viper could decide the tighter teamfights. Viper went 7/1/8 on Ezreal in Game 3 against T1, putting BLG ahead for good. Against Gen.G, ON and Bin can give him room to deal damage by starting fights before Ruler is in position.
 Under Fearless Draft , champions picked in one game are unavailable to both teams for the rest of the series. If the final reaches Game 4 or 5, both teams will have fewer options for starting fights and protecting their bot carries.
 Gen.G vs BLG Betting Odds and Key Markets

 Match Winner
 Gen.G are favourites after winning every series at Worlds. Their comeback against Invictus Gaming matters here because BLG can put them under early pressure. BLG’s path to an upset is to turn that pressure into objectives and keep Gen.G from stabilizing the game around Baron.

 Map Handicap
 Gen.G −1.5 requires a 3–0 or 3–1 win . The two knockout sweeps make that margin plausible, but the handicap gives Gen.G room to drop only one game. BLG +1.5 covers any BLG series win or a 3–2 loss. A fifth game would therefore be enough for BLG to cover even if Gen.G wins the title.

 Total Maps (Over/Under 3.5)
 Over 3.5 lands if both teams win at least one game. Under 3.5 requires a sweep by either finalist. Three of their four previous international best-of-fives went to at least four games. The 1.30 price reflects how strongly Stake favours that outcome, even with Gen.G coming off two 3–0 wins.

 LoL Worlds 2026 Final Start Time and Where to Watch in Canada
 The final is scheduled for Saturday, November 14 at 2 p.m. ET at Barclays Center. That’s 11 a.m. PT in Vancouver, noon MT in Calgary, 1 p.m. CT in Winnipeg, 3 p.m. AT in Halifax and 3:30 p.m. NT in St. John’s. The series will stream on LoL Esports, YouTube and Twitch.
 Gen.G vs BLG Final Prediction and Best Bet
 Best bet — Gen.G to win at 1.55. Predicted score — Gen.G 3–1. Gen.G’s edge is their ability to win games from different positions. They can play through Chovy when he gets the first move out of mid, and the Invictus semifinal showed they can still find a winning fight when the early game goes against them.
 This preview is based on tournament results, head-to-head history and the information available at the time of writing.
